heuristics.statement: The real r=23 walk map F(x) = digest(message(x+rho0))*LAMBDA with a fresh random rho0 finds a collision with probability at least 0.39 at the filed budget n1 = 172533624524770551326248201244353529883 = ceil(m_hi * n0), where n0 = 169183785570475143485240440522017581764 is the tight uniform-random-function budget for 0.39 and m_hi = 1.0198 is the profile-likelihood 95% upper bound of the measured first-repeat hazard multiplier. Equivalently: the real map's first-repeat hazard is at most m_hi times the random-function rate.
heuristics.scope: The exact r=23 Orchard Poseidon permutation with pinned deployed constants; walk values in Z_p; fresh rho0 uniform on 254 bits and fresh start per walk; first-repeat statistics only.
heuristics.extrapolation: Measured on the same r=23 map truncated to w in [16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36] bits (fresh truncated start per walk, exact discrete first-repeat likelihood with bounded series tail, profile-likelihood interval); pooled hazard multiplier 1.0044, 95% CI [0.9891, 1.0198], 16380 walks over six widths. The filed budget n1 = ceil(m_hi * n0) dominates every hazard value inside the measured 95% interval.
heuristics.limitations: No proof of H1 is known. The measurements are reduced-width only; the full-width first-repeat cannot be observed. The 14-bit organizer event cannot separate hazard multipliers near 0.5 from 1. The interval is conditional on the hazard-multiplier family, per-walk seed independence, and the exact-discrete likelihood tail bound; profile-likelihood coverage is calibrated by simulation, not exact. If the real map's hazard exceeded m_hi the filed success probability would fall below 0.39 by the corresponding factor.
